text:
Alex L: Quick check — we're finalizing the rerank endpoint contract for v2. Main questions: score semantics (higher is better?), tie-breaking, and backward compatibility for clients that rely on stable ordering. Pasting a minimal proposal below, open to bikeshedding. cc @Samir @Maria G

Alex L: ```json
{
  "request": {
    "query": "...",
    "candidates": [{ "id": "c1", "text": "..." }],
    "tie_breaker": "deterministic|random"  // optional override
  },
  "response": [{ "id": "c1", "score": 0.87, "normalized_score": 0.87 }]
}
```

Samir: higher == better. We should be explicit: score is a float, positive = better. But legacy models sometimes emit >1 or unbounded logits. Two options: 1) require model-side normalization (recommended), or 2) accept any float and add an optional `normalized_score` in response when available.

Maria G: prefer option (2). Don't break older exporters. Proposal: require `score` (float, can be any finite number), optional `normalized_score` in [0,1] when model/runtime can provide it. Document: clients must treat higher as better; server will NOT implicitly rescale arbitrary scores.

Ciara: We rely on stable order for pagination/continuations — default must be deterministic. Suggest default tie-breaker = lexicographic `id` ascending when scores equal, unless request sets `tie_breaker: random` with a seed. Also define null/NaN handling: treat null/NaN as lowest possible value (i.e., sorted last).

Alex L: Sounds good. I'll update the JSON schema accordingly: 1) `score` required (number), 2) `normalized_score` optional (number 0..1), 3) server computes `rank` when returning but `rank` is not accepted in request, 4) default tie-break: score desc, then id lexicographic asc. Add `tie_break_seed` optional for deterministic shuffle.

Alex L: Sample response we can publish in docs:```json
[
  {
    "id": "doc-42",
    "score": 12.3,
    "normalized_score": 0.94,
    "metadata": { "source": "kb" },
    "rank": 1
  },
  {
    "id": "doc-7",
    "score": 12.3,
    "normalized_score": 0.94,
    "rank": 2  // tie resolved by id (doc-42 < doc-7?) see note below
  }
]
```
(note: rank is server-provided; clients should not send `rank`)

Samir: minor nit: clarify lexicographic order direction. I vote id ascending (a..z) after score desc. Also call out behavior when `normalized_score` present: it is purely advisory and may be used by clients for UI.

Maria G: add compatibility rule: if a future change needs to flip default tie-breaker, must go through a 6-week deprecation window and a feature flag on server to preserve old behavior for clients.

Ciara: I'll add an integration test that simulates identical scores from model and asserts deterministic ordering by id, plus a test that sends `tie_breaker: random` with seed and verifies stable shuffle.

Samir: Also add an edge-case test for NaN/Inf in `score`. Ensure runtime converts Inf -> null and NaN -> null, and we document that `null` scores sort last.

Alex L: Great. I'll open a small PR with the schema changes, sample responses, and changelog entry. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/314 (draft). Planning canary on dedicated for the API shape change, no model migration required.

Samir: LGTM, thanks. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: canary deploy scheduled 2026-03-19T03:00:00Z for api/v2-rerank-shape

Ciara: I'll add a short note in the changelog and ping support about the compatibility window.

Alex L: thanks all — I'll update the doc and ping again once PR is ready for review.
